description.narrative: The project will support the government's transport sector priorities to enhance connectivity and efficient movement in the Greater Mekong Subregion (GMS) through national and provincial road rehabilitation and development. The project will also help improve axle load control and strengthen awareness of road safety and potential social problems.

description.narrative: Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Awareness of road safety and potential social problems strengthened Indicator: 60% of community residents (at least 40% of whom are women) report improved knowledge and understanding of road safety measures, HIV/AIDS, human trafficking, GBV-SEAH, and sexual and reproductive health. (2021 baseline: 0%) (OP 2.2.3) Achievement: 32.07 Progress/Status: Activities are ongoing. As of 30 Nov 2025, (the latest report available), various training-workshop and public fora for road safety awareness were conducted by the Consultant in the project areas. The participants comprised of students, community members and vehicle operators and drivers. Out of the target 14,447 persons, a total of 8,939 persons (61.88%) had participated in the activities since consultant mobilization. Out of this number, 4,811 were females or 83.25% of the target 5,779 females (40% of 14,447).
The EA will recruit a team of consultants to implement GBV-SEAH and human trafficking activities. Data Source: Project progress report

Output: Awareness of road safety and potential social problems strengthened Indicator: Gender-responsive road safety technologies introduced to improve access to information and services for road safety, HIV/AIDS, human trafficking, GBV-SEAH, and sexual and reproductive health. (2021 baseline: 0%) (OP 6.2.1, OP 2.2.3) Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: The EA will recruit a team of consultants to implement GBV-SEAH and human trafficking activities. Data Source: Project progress report

Output: National and provincial road sections improved with climate-resilient designs Indicator: About 48 km of national and provincial road network improved to three stars or above (2021 baseline: 0 km) (OP 2.4.1, OP 3.2.1, OP 3.2.5, OP 6.2.1) Achievement: 28 Progress/Status: As of 31 December 2025, the project overall progress is 87.2% with a time elapsed of 55.3%. The progress under each output is described below.
Output 1: Improvement works for CW-1 NR23 were completed. Maintenance works commenced on 1 October 2025 with 8.3% progress by end of December 2025. Actual overall progress is 87.86%. For CW-2 PR312, improvement works progress is 99.00%. Maintenance works for CW-2 commenced in February 2025 with 28.6% progress by end December 2025. Actual overall progress is 88.5%.
All two goods contracts under this Output have been awarded and completed by January 2024.
Data Source: Construction completion report

Output: National and provincial road sections improved with climate-resilient designs Indicator: About 48 km of performance-based maintenance undertaken using labor contracting society contracts, with at least 30% women's participation in cumulative labor days (2021 baseline: 0 km) (OP 2.1) Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Construction works are completed for NR23. Maintenance works have commenced with 8.3% progress as of Dec 2025. For PR312, construction works are still ongoing in the remaining road section. Maintenance works commenced in February 2025 and progress to date is 28.6% Data Source: Construction completion report and project progress report

Output: National and provincial road sections improved with climate-resilient designs Indicator: Women hired by contractors in construction phase for at least 20% of cumulative labor days (2021 baseline: 0%) Achievement: 23.63 Progress/Status: As of 31 Oct 2025, the cumulative person-days of hired skilled and unskilled labor during the construction phase performed by women was 44,131 labor days, equal to 25.19%. This is over the target of 20%.
Data Source: Construction completion report and project progress report

Output: Axle load control enhanced Indicator: Weigh scales, equipment, and vehicles for four mobile teams provided and teams operational (2021 baseline: two mobile teams) (OP 6.2.1) Achievement: 2 Progress/Status: Mobile team vehicles and axle load control equipment (EQ-1) have been procured. Certificate of final acceptance was issued to the supplier on 4 August 2023. The four mobile teams have been operational since 19 September 2023. Data Source: Project progress report
